label: Can afford pillar

fields.name: Arg0

fields.values: a culture pillar, vanilla passes CulturePillar.Self

details: Vanilla shows it in the cost tooltip, under the line with the total cost (GetCostString).

details: Vanilla shows it as 'Cost: …' in the window and at the top of the cost tooltip.

label: Pick blockers

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture pillar offered as a replacement.
fields.values: a culture pillar, vanilla passes CulturePillar.Self

label: Pillar cost breakdown

fields.name: Arg0

fields.values: a culture pillar, vanilla passes CulturePillar.Self

label: Pillar cost

fields.name: Arg0

label: Possible pillars

label: Select pillar
summary: Chooses the given culture pillar as the replacement in the window.

details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; decision texts use the same name on a faith, for example 'accept [it] love'; that is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: High god: herself/himself
summary: Going by its name, 'herself' or 'himself' to fit the rite's high god.
details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; decision and game rule texts use the same name on a faith, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: High god name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the rite's high god.
details: Vanilla never names it on a rite. The same name on a faith is one of the most used functions in the game's texts; that is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: High god name (2)
summary: Going by its name, a second form of the name of the rite's high god.
details: No game text uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: High god other name
summary: Going by its name, another name for the rite's high god.
details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; decision texts use the same name on a faith, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: High god other name's
summary: Going by its name, the possessive form of the other name of the rite's high god.
details: Vanilla never names it on a rite. An event title uses the same name on a faith: '[it] Wrath'; that is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: High god name's
summary: Going by its name, the possessive form of the name of the rite's high god.
details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; decision and game rule texts use the same name on a faith, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; event and tradition texts use the same name on a faith, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; game texts use the same name on a faith, for example 'a humble wayside [it]'; that is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: House of worship (2)
summary: Going by its name, a second word for the rite's place of worship.
details: No game text uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: House of worship (3)
summary: Going by its name, a third word for the rite's place of worship.
details: No game text uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Houses of worship
summary: Going by its name, the rite's word for places of worship, in the plural.
details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; a decision and an event text use the same name on a faith, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Household god: her/him
summary: Going by its name, the pronoun 'her' or 'him' that fits the rite's household god.
details: No game text uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Household god: her/his
summary: Going by its name, the possessive 'her' or 'his' that fits the rite's household god.
details: No game text uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Household god name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the rite's household god (the god of home and family).
details: Vanilla never names it on a rite; board game and accolade texts use the same name on a faith, which is only a hint. The game documents no return type.

label: Household god name's
summary: Going by its name, the possessive form of the name of the rite's household god.
details: No game text uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Household god: she/he
summary: Going by its name, the pronoun 'she' or 'he' that fits the rite's household god.
details: No game text uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Conversion allowed
summary: Going by its name, whether converting to the rite is allowed.
details: Vanilla never uses it. The game documents nothing more.

label: Is enabled
summary: Going by its name, whether the rite is enabled.
details: Vanilla never uses it on a rite; the lines with the same name belong to the music player and are only a hint. What enabled means for a rite is not shown.

label: Is historical only
summary: Whether the rite exists only for history, so players cannot convert to it or design a ruler with it.
details: Vanilla hides the convert button, the 'find a character of this faith' option and the ruler designer choice for such a rite.

label: Is main rite
summary: Whether the rite is its faith's main (mainline) rite rather than a branch.
details: Vanilla shows the rite's status as main or branch in the faith view from it.

label: Is selected
summary: Going by its name, whether the rite is the one selected in a list.
details: Vanilla never uses it on a rite; the lines with the same name belong to other list items and are only a hint.

label: Is trait a sin
summary: Whether the rite counts the given trait as a sin.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch on the sin version of a trait icon. IsTraitVirtue is the matching check for virtues.

label: Is trait a virtue
summary: Whether the rite counts the given trait as a virtue.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch on the virtue version of a trait icon (with a green glow). IsTraitSin is the matching check for sins.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether there is a rite here at all.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of a notification only when a rite is set.
